prompt: rgb.jpg is a horizontal strip of 5 frames, left to right in time order, sampled from the few seconds of a head-mounted (egocentric) video; the camera wearer is the viewpoint. depth.jpg, segmentation.jpg and pose.jpg are the same 5 frames rendered as a monocular depth map (brighter = nearer to the camera wearer), an instance segmentation map (coloured masks with class labels), and a body/hand skeleton map (yellow = body, magenta = hands) on black. Look at all four images. For EACH of the three maps, describe the spatial understanding that map supports, using the RGB strip for context: the layout of the scene; which people and objects are present and roughly how far each is from the camera wearer (in metres) and from each other; relative positions (left/right/in front/behind, above/below); which way people face and whether they look toward the camera wearer; what is within arm's reach of the camera wearer or of others; occlusions and anything partly out of view; and how these change across the 5 frames (approach, retreat, turning). Say what each map shows that is hard to see in the RGB alone, and where the map looks unreliable. Describe only spatial facts. Do not guess anyone's intentions, social norms, or what anyone should do. Return only JSON: {"depth": "...", "segmentation": "...", "pose": "..."} with 3-5 sentences each.

descriptions.depth: The depth map shows a top-down view of a kitchen counter and double sink roughly 0.5–0.9 m below and in front of the camera wearer, with a darker floor area (around 1.2–1.5 m away) on the left where a second person in pink pajamas stands about 0.8–1.2 m to the left and slightly behind the wearer. Bright foreground silhouettes (0.2–0.6 m) track the camera wearer's arms within arm's reach as the left hand moves from a wooden cutting board (frame 1) into a metal bowl of raw chicken (frame 2, ~0.2 m to the right of the board), and then both hands move rightward over the right sink basin (frames 3–5, ~0.4 m further right) as the wearer turns right and then pans left in frame 5. As the camera shifts across the frames, the second person goes from mostly occluded at the bottom-left edge (frames 1–3) to standing clearly on the floor in frame 5 facing toward the counter/wearer's left side while holding a phone near their face without looking up at the camera. Compared to RGB alone, the depth map clearly separates the vertical height step between the raised counter surface, the recessed sink basins containing dark pots, and the lower kitchen floor. However, the depth map is unreliable around the curved faucet neck in frame 4 (blending it into the background wall) and loses fine internal geometry inside the dark pots and along the second person's blurred head in frame 5.
descriptions.segmentation: The segmentation map labels parts of the scene across the 5 frames, identifying the counter surface as a 'dining table' in frame 1 (0.5–0.9 m away), two 'bowl' instances (the large metal bowl of chicken at ~0.5 m and a smaller green bowl behind it at ~0.7 m, about 0.15 m apart), a 'bottle' behind the sink (~0.7–0.8 m away), and 'person' masks for both the camera wearer's arms (0.2–0.6 m) and the second person standing on the left (0.8–1.2 m away). In frames 1–4, the camera wearer's lower body and the second person's torso are mostly out of view below the bottom-left frame edge, while in frame 5 the second person is fully segmented in light blue to the left of the brown mask of the wearer's outstretched arms over the sink, facing right toward the counter with a phone occluding part of their chest and face. Everything on the counter—the cutting board, knife, metal bowl, and sink pots—is within arm's reach of the camera wearer, whereas the phone is within arm's reach of the second person's hands. When it succeeds, the segmentation map isolates discrete object boundaries such as the foreground arm masks and the circular rim of the chicken bowl against cluttered countertop textures. However, it is highly unreliable across the strip: it misclassifies the kitchen counter as a dining table in frame 1, fails to detect the counter, bowls, pots, cutting board, and knife in frames 2–4, and merges the camera wearer's two arms and torso into a single undifferentiated person mask.
descriptions.pose: The pose map is almost completely black across all 5 frames, detecting only a single magenta hand skeleton for the camera wearer's left hand in frame 1 (at the cutting board, ~0.5 m away on the left) and in frame 4 (at the sink basin, ~0.5 m away near the center-right). In the RGB context, the camera wearer's left hand is within arm's reach of the chicken on the cutting board in frame 1 and meets the right hand at the sink edge in frame 4, while the second person stands 0.8–1.2 m to the left on the floor, facing toward the counter in frame 5 with both hands raised to hold a phone rather than looking at the camera wearer. When detected in frames 1 and 4, the magenta wireframe makes the exact finger articulation and downward wrist orientation of the wearer's grasping left hand easier to see than in the motion-blurred RGB frames. However, the pose map is severely unreliable overall: it completely misses all yellow body skeletons for both the camera wearer and the second person across all 5 frames, fails to detect the wearer's right hand in frames 1–5 and left hand in frames 2, 3, and 5, and misses the second person's hands holding the phone in frames 1, 2, and 5 despite being visible in RGB.
